Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test `testBoundaryRangeTooLarge()` attempts to use the CMAESOptimizer with very wide bounds close to half of the max double value. According to the current bug report, this results in NaN parameters being passed to the fitness function.

Looking at the `CMAESOptimizer.doOptimize()` method, the optimization process uses a `FitnessFunction` object to encode and decode solution points between the internal normalized representation and the real problem bounds.

The `FitnessFunction.encode(double[] x)` method normalizes a parameter by subtracting the lower bound and dividing by the difference between upper and lower bounds. Similarly, the `decode` method reverses this by multiplying the normalized value by the difference and adding the lower bound back.

The key problem is that when the bounds are excessively large (close to Double.MAX_VALUE, e.g., half of it or more), the difference computed as `boundaries[1][i] - boundaries[0][i]` can overflow or become too large. This leads to computations that end up producing NaN values during either encoding (normalizing input parameters) or decoding (denormalizing candidate solutions back to real bounds).

Since the internal logic of CMAESOptimizer relies on these normalized parameters, any NaN propagation to the fitness function causes failures or exceptions.

Hence, the root cause is the lack of safeguards against excessive boundary ranges in the encode/decode methods of the FitnessFunction. The normalization step on extremely wide bounds produces NaNs that propagate into the optimization process and the fitness function evaluation.

Additionally, the first recent bug report indicates other issues with bound enforcement which might be related, but our primary diagnosis revolves around the normalization logic overflow in encode/decode.

To fix the issue, the optimizer should validate and reject overly wide boundary ranges early or handle the normalization more safely to prevent NaNs.

This explains why the test which provides extremely wide bounds fails with NaN parameters in the fitness function.

Summary:
- Test uses very wide bounds near max double values.
- FitnessFunction.encode/decode normalize using difference of bounds.
- Wide bounds difference overflows or produces NaN in normalization.
- NaN parameters passed to fitness function cause failure.
- Lack of range checks or protections in encode/decode is root cause.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
